title: Reincarnated as Expendable: The Misadventures of Fred Mai-Captain
author: McSloth
blurb:
Reincarnated as Expendable: The Misadventures of Fred Mai-Captain. A standalone fantasy satire of about 20 chapters.
Fred Mai-Captain is a night-shift convenience-store clerk whose only ambition is to make Shift Supervisor. Then a truck marked "Fekfosio Recruitment Services" runs him down.
He wakes in the processing hall of Goddess Facilmora, a reincarnation manager far behind on quota, who stamps him through in seconds. His cheat skill is Always Finds Socks. His Status Screen misfiles him as "Latrine Paladin, Lv. 1," and his surname crashes the rank field. Beside him in the queue, a handsome young man named Kaito Reklamo receives a holy sword, infinite mana and a harem.
The Holy Kingdom of Fekfosio runs on one industry: summoning Heroes from Earth to fight an endless war against the Demon Lord. A few Chosen Ones are the face of the war. Everyone else, tens of thousands of them, does the cleaning, the fighting and the dying.
At boot camp, Sergeant Gangrene Gruk renames Fred "Recruit Hyphen" and promises he'll make captain "when demons fly." Quartermaster Bilge Reprobate sells Fred his own boots. Fred befriends Mook Moreover, a former accountant who opens every sentence with "Moreover." At graduation Kaito is showered in petals, and Fred is issued a rusty sword and a mop.
Fred is assigned to Kaito's party as Sanitation Support. A general mistakes his name for his rank and puts him in charge of a doomed charge. Fred's mop accidentally wins the battle, and Mook is killed. Sister Verna Walleye, a healer who has failed her eye exam eleven times, gives Fred an orc's arm by mistake. The victory is credited to Kaito, and Fred is fined for the mop.
On leave in the capital, Fred spends weeks lost in a city that is one vast building of forms, and he comes out knowing them better than anyone. He's arrested for impersonating an officer. When he appeals his misfiled class, he discovers the truth. The Bureau of Destiny picks its Chosen Ones by marketing focus group, Kaito's legendary feats are staged, and Kaito himself is miserable and contractually bound to smile. Being Chosen is a product, and the war is its advertising. Fred is court-martialed for leaking the truth and sentenced to the Demon Front.
The demons capture him (demons, it turns out, fly). Their realm is the same machine with horns, and Mook is there, re-summoned as a demon. Demon General Malingering Mortuus, forever trying to get signed off sick, admits that both sides need the war, because without it there's nothing to sell. Fred meets the Demon Lord, who turns out to be a committee, and is traded back in a prisoner exchange.
Presumed dead, Fred gets home in time to hear himself eulogized as "Captain Mai-Captain," complete with lines from "O Captain! My Captain!" He walks in alive, and the posthumous promotion stands.
Posted to the Summoning Bureau, Captain Mai-Captain looks every inch the loyal officer. A terrified new arrival stammers, "Captain... Mai-Captain?" Fred returns the salute, then quietly stamps the boy's file "Returned to Sender" and sends him home. One down, ten thousand to go.
